reason: The text does not demonstrate that Yahweh becomes angry when the people voice their opinions and feelings. In multiple instances, the people explicitly voice their opinions and affirmations (Exodus 19:8: 'All that the LORD has spoken we will do'; Exodus 24:3, 24:7: similar affirmations) without provoking Yahweh's anger. When the people voice fear and hesitation (Exodus 20:18-19, asking Moses to speak to them instead of God), Yahweh does not respond with anger. Yahweh's anger in this passage is specifically directed at the people's creation and worship of the Golden Calf (Exodus 32), which is an act of idolatry and corruption ('your people have acted perversely'), not at the mere act of voicing opinions or expressing feelings.
